description: Prettier code formatter integration for Neovim. Formats JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, HTML, JSON, YAML, Markdown, and more using the Prettier CLI. Works standalone without null-ls — provides the :Prettier command and plug mappings. Optionally integrates with null-ls.nvim if installed.
author: MunifTanjim

options.label: Formatter Binary
options.description: Which Prettier binary to use. 'prettier' is the standard CLI tool. 'prettierd' is a faster daemon that persists between runs (requires prettierd v0.23.3+ installed separately).

options.label: Filetypes
options.description: List of Neovim filetypes that prettier.nvim will register as a formatter for. Remove any filetypes you don't want Prettier to handle.

options.label: Print Width
options.description: Target line length Prettier will try to wrap at. This is a soft limit — Prettier may produce shorter or longer lines as needed for correctness.

options.label: Tab Width
options.description: Number of spaces per indentation level.

options.label: Use Tabs
options.description: Indent with tabs instead of spaces. When enabled, Tab Width still controls alignment (Prettier uses SmartTabs behavior).

options.label: Semicolons
options.description: Print semicolons at the end of every statement. When disabled, semicolons are only added where required to prevent ASI failures.

options.label: Single Quotes
options.description: Use single quotes instead of double quotes in JavaScript and TypeScript. JSX always uses double quotes regardless of this setting.

options.label: Trailing Commas
options.description: Controls where Prettier adds trailing commas in multi-line structures. 'All' is the Prettier v3 default (ES2017+). 'ES5' is the Prettier v2 default. 'None' never adds trailing commas.

options.label: ES5 (objects, arrays only, Prettier v2 default)
Bracket Spacing
options.description: Print spaces between brackets in object literals. When enabled: { foo: bar }. When disabled: {foo: bar}.

options.label: Bracket Same Line
options.description: Put the closing '>' of a multi-line HTML/JSX element on the same line as the last attribute rather than on its own line.

options.label: JSX Bracket Same Line
options.description: JSX-specific: put the closing '>' of a multi-line JSX opening tag on the same line as the last prop. This option applies only to JSX, while Bracket Same Line applies to HTML and other formats.

options.label: JSX Single Quotes
options.description: Use single quotes instead of double quotes in JSX attributes. This setting applies only to JSX, regardless of the main Single Quotes setting.

options.label: Quote Props
options.description: When to add quotes around object property names. 'As Needed' only quotes properties that require it. 'Consistent' quotes all if any requires it. 'Preserve' respects the input.

options.label: Consistent (quote all if any needs quotes)
Arrow Function Parentheses
options.description: Include parentheses around a sole arrow function parameter. 'Always': (x) => x. 'Avoid': x => x.

options.label: Single Attribute Per Line
options.description: Enforce one attribute per line in HTML, Vue, and JSX elements.

options.label: Prose Wrap
options.description: How to wrap prose in Markdown files. 'Preserve' leaves existing line breaks unchanged. 'Always' wraps at print width. 'Never' puts each paragraph on a single line.

options.label: HTML Whitespace Sensitivity
options.description: Whitespace handling in HTML, Vue, Angular, and Handlebars. 'CSS' respects CSS display rules. 'Strict' treats all tag whitespace as significant. 'Ignore' treats it as insignificant.

options.label: Embedded Language Formatting
options.description: Whether Prettier should format code embedded in template literals or Markdown code blocks. 'Auto' attempts to detect and format. 'Off' disables this feature.

options.label: End of Line
options.description: Line ending style. 'LF' is standard on Linux/macOS and in git repos. 'CRLF' is standard on Windows. 'Auto' maintains existing line endings.

options.label: Vue: Indent Script and Style
options.description: Indent the code inside <script> and <style> tags in Vue single-file components.

options.label: Config Precedence
options.description: Controls how CLI options interact with project-level Prettier config files (.prettierrc, etc.). 'Prefer File' uses CLI options only when no config file is found. 'CLI Override' always applies CLI options on top of any file config. 'File Override' always lets the config file win.

options.label: Prefer File (CLI options as fallback only)

functions.name: format
functions.label: Format Buffer
functions.description: Format the current buffer with Prettier
functions.whatItDoes: Triggers Prettier to format the entire current buffer using the plugin's own API. Equivalent to running :Prettier. Works in standalone mode — no null-ls required.

functions.name: format_range
functions.label: Format Range
functions.description: Format the current visual selection with Prettier
functions.whatItDoes: Triggers Prettier range formatting for the currently selected lines. Use this in visual mode mappings. Works in standalone mode — no null-ls required.

functions.name: config_exists
functions.label: Check Config Exists
functions.description: Check whether a Prettier configuration file exists in the current project
functions.whatItDoes: Returns true if a Prettier config file (.prettierrc, prettier.config.js, or 'prettier' key in package.json) is found in the project directory. Useful for conditionally enabling formatting.

params.name: check_package_json
params.description: Also check package.json for a 'prettier' key (default: true)

functionTemplates.label: Format on Save
functionTemplates.shortDescription: Run :Prettier on the buffer — wire to BufWritePre for auto-format on save
functionTemplates.whatItDoes: Invokes the :Prettier command to format the current buffer. Connect this to a BufWritePre trigger node in the graph editor to auto-format every time you save a file. Uses the standalone prettier.nvim command path — no null-ls required.

exCommands.name: Prettier
exCommands.description: Format the current buffer with Prettier. Works in both normal mode (full buffer) and visual mode (selected range). This is the primary interface for prettier.nvim in standalone mode (no null-ls).
